title: Improving cross-lingual dependency parsing via LLM-based transferring and self-optimizing synthetic data augmentation
note: The authors combine cross-lingual transfer with feedback from a dependency parser to generate training trees for four low-resource languages.

title: Universal constituency treebanking and parsing: A pilot study
note: The authors align phrase labels across languages and use LLM-derived syntactic knowledge to convert dependency trees into constituency training data.

title: Better Benchmarking LLMs for Zero-Shot Dependency Parsing
note: The study compares open-weight models with baselines that construct trees without seeing the sentence, including randomly sampled projective trees.

title: Branching Out: Exploration of Chinese Dependency Parsing with Fine-tuned Large Language Models
note: Different encodings for training Chinese Llama-3 change both how often it produces a valid tree and how accurately it attaches words.

title: Constituency Parsing Using LLMs
note: The authors compare prompting and supervised training for tree generation, then study how learning from errors and revising outputs affect tree validity.

title: Contrastive Learning on LLM Back Generation Treebank for Cross-domain Constituency Parsing
note: An LLM fills gaps in phrase trees that contain domain keywords, creating training examples for a parser that learns to distinguish spans.

title: Cross-Domain Constituency Parsing with Multi-LLM Debate
note: Several models fine-tuned on a small source-domain sample debate their proposed analyses over multiple rounds to parse sentences from a new domain.

title: Hybrid Human-LLM Corpus Construction and LLM Evaluation for the Caused-Motion Construction
note: Dependency parsing and LLM assistance help annotators collect examples in which a sentence describes one participant causing another to move.

title: LLM Dependency Parsing with In-Context Rules
note: Across eight low-resource languages, rules improved zero-shot parsing, but adding them yielded no further benefit once the prompt included labeled examples.

title: Memory-enhanced Large Language Model for Cross-lingual Dependency Parsing via Deep Hierarchical Syntax Understanding
note: Multitask training produces an initial parse, then multilingual tables of dependency labels guide the model on relations it handles poorly.

title: Parsing the Switch: LLM-Based UD Annotation for Complex Code-Switched and Low-Resource Languages
note: Experts revise LLM-generated dependency trees to build annotated corpora for Spanish–English and Spanish–Guaraní code-switching.

title: Pre-annotation Matters: A Comparative Study on POS and Dependency Annotation for an Alsatian Dialect
note: For an Alsatian dialect, the authors compare three ways to draft part-of-speech tags and dependency trees before annotators correct them.

title: Self-Correction Makes LLMs Better Parsers
note: A checker flags possible errors in a proposed tree and retrieves grammar rules and examples that guide the model’s next revision.

title: Step-by-step Instructions and a Simple Tabular Output Format Improve the Dependency Parsing Accuracy of LLMs
note: The parser first assigns part-of-speech tags, then writes each word’s head and relation in a simplified table tested across 17 languages.

title: Dependency Annotation of Ottoman Turkish with Multilingual BERT
note: Annotators correct a multilingual BERT parser’s draft trees and use the corrections to retrain it as they build an Ottoman Turkish treebank.

title: Large Language Models Are No Longer Shallow Parsers
note: The model identifies short phrases, filters unreliable chunks and uses the remaining phrases to build a full English or Chinese parse tree.

title: LLM-Assisted Data Augmentation for Chinese Dialogue-Level Dependency Parsing
note: The authors vary words, syntax and discourse structure in Chinese dialogues to train a parser on dependencies within and across discourse units.

title: Sketch-Guided Constrained Decoding for Boosting Blackbox Large Language Models without Logit Access
note: A black-box model drafts the parse and a local model revises that draft under grammar constraints.

title: U-DepPLLaMA: Universal Dependency Parsing via Auto-regressive Large Language Models
note: U-DepPLLaMA learns to generate a bracketed sequence encoding a sentence’s dependency tree.

title: BenchCLAMP: A Benchmark for Evaluating Language Models on Syntactic and Semantic Parsing
note: The benchmark compares constrained generation on Penn Treebank constituency trees and English Web Treebank dependencies across several amounts of training data.

title: ChatGPT is a Potential Zero-Shot Dependency Parser
note: The authors ask ChatGPT to produce dependency analyses without worked examples and examine which syntactic relations it tends to predict.

title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured NLP Tasks without Finetuning
note: An input-dependent grammar restricts which tokens the model can generate as it writes a constituency tree.

title: LLM-enhanced Self-training for Cross-domain Constituency Parsing
note: Grammar rules guide an LLM to generate target-domain sentences, which a parser labels and filters for its next round of training.

title: Improving Constituency Parsing with Span Attention
note: The parser weights n-grams inside each candidate constituent, adding evidence from the interior of a phrase to its boundary representation.

title: 75 Languages, 1 Model: Parsing Universal Dependencies Universally
note: UDify fine-tunes a shared multilingual BERT encoder on 124 treebanks to predict dependency trees alongside morphology, lemmas, and part-of-speech tags.

title: Reinforced Training Data Selection for Domain Adaptation
note: A reinforcement learning system chooses training examples suited to a target domain, with dependency parsing among its evaluation tasks.

title: Constituency Parsing with a Self-Attentive Encoder
note: A chart parser uses self-attention to represent words in context and investigates how word content and position contribute to phrase recognition.

title: A Minimal Span-Based Neural Constituency Parser
note: A neural model scores spans and their labels independently, supporting both exact chart search and greedy top-down parsing.

title: Stanford’s Graph-based Neural Dependency Parser at the CoNLL 2017 Shared Task
note: A graph-based parser scores possible heads and dependency labels using contextual word representations that include character information.

title: Simple and Accurate Dependency Parsing Using Bidirectional LSTM Feature Representations
note: The authors use the same bidirectional LSTM feature design in a greedy transition parser and a globally optimized graph parser.

title: Grammar as a Foreign Language
note: An attention-based encoder–decoder generates a phrase-structure tree as a sequence of symbols.

title: Cross Language Dependency Parsing using a Bilingual Lexicon
note: A bilingual dictionary supplies word-level translations of an annotated treebank so its dependency structures can help train a parser in another language.

title: Algorithms for Deterministic Incremental Dependency Parsing
note: This study compares four transition systems for building dependencies incrementally and analyzes which trees each can construct.

title: Learning Accurate, Compact, and Interpretable Tree Annotation
note: A split-and-merge procedure learns finer grammatical categories from treebank examples while retaining familiar phrase labels in the output.

title: Online Large-Margin Training of Dependency Parsers
note: An online learning algorithm adjusts arc weights so that the gold dependency tree scores above competing trees.

title: Three Generative, Lexicalised Models for Statistical Parsing
note: The models generate phrase structure around lexical heads and progressively account for argument patterns and displaced constituents.

title: Three New Probabilistic Models for Dependency Parsing: An Exploration
note: A cubic-time algorithm finds projective dependency trees and provides a common decoder for three probabilistic models.
